quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: What do you consider "closest to the sun in color"?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is what they call "Cor Lapis."

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, it is so warm... it smells so good and feels so soft — it truly is as gentle as the sun itself. Surely, humans must use these to make food? Anyway, thank you so much. I will remember this item.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How... were you able to see all that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. What are you doing here all by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Gah! Don't suddenly talk to people while standing behind them! You almost made me scatter this powder...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Powder? Err, what's this stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Gems!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gems? But why would there be any here?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Wouldn't it be stranger to not find them here? I mean, this is my workshop, in which I process gems... Although I must admit that it doesn't have an official name yet.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: I did consider calling it "Studio Sluasi" in the past, but I'm not sure if using my name so directly is such a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean by "processing gems"?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: That means that I turn gems into various pretty ornaments... and stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, I won't be able to take new commissions for a while. I need to concentrate on making paints... Well, I am still using gems for that, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're gonna make paints out of gems? Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Yes. What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, well, it just feels like a waste... You could just give them to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But still, why do you need to make paints? Paimon's pretty sure there's no such step in using gems to make ornaments, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Well, a child who loves painting came to ask me if I could make paints as shiny as gems and as bright as the sun.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Moreover, she recently saved my younger sister when the village was shaking very violently.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: That's why I've decided to try to fulfill her wish by creating a "paint as bright as the sun" and giving it to her as a thank-you gift.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, you must be referring to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the girl who enjoys painting you spoke of named Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Hmm? Yes... Do you two know her?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Sluasi about your previous experiences with Mamere...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: So... So the two of you are the esteemed ones who saved Puca alongside Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Esteemed ones...?

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Thank you. Thank you both so much! If it weren't for you, Puca might have been...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Please, take these... If you don't mind, that is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Can we really take them, {NICKNAME}? They look really expensive...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon didn't think Mamere would go commission people of her own accord...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Well, she didn't really commission me to do anything, did she? She just asked if I could do it. In fact, she ran off before I could even reply...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... Yeah. That sounds like something she would do.

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: #Speaking of which, esteemed {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: What would you call "the closest thing to the sun in color"?

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: I have tried to observe the sun myself, but I am not sure what materials I should use to recreate its tones...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... "closest to the sun in color," you say...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Well, Canotila did tell me once that "gold is the tears of the sun," or something like that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But wouldn't that be way too luxurious? There has to be something more normal we could use...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just think. We have to have seen something that most "resembles in the sun in color" and that can be found just about anywhere...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: ...That is true. The closest thing to the sun is indeed the sun itself.

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: But how do I grind the sun into powder, I wonder...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Are you seriously discussing something this ridiculous?

choices.text: In that case, you could probably use my hair...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: ...Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, you can't use hair to make paints!

choices.text: I wouldn't call us the "esteemed" anything...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: What do you consider <color=#00E1FFFF>"closest to the sun in color"</color>?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sluasi carefully checks the material before handing them back to you...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, thank you two for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: #However, I cannot simply take what is yours, esteemed {NICKNAME}. Thus, I shall simply learn the name of that material from you, and I shall later set out to find it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Still, would you not say that this color is a bit too... intense?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: The "color of the sun" should have a lighter touch, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you mean that it should lean further toward being "white"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. The "sun" is more "white" than it is "gold"...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: "White," you say? However, I am not sure what materials we must use to achieve this lighter shade...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: I have tried that in the past... but it did not turn out so well. Colors produced that way turn out rather murky — they lack the striking brilliance the sun has...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: So it would be best if we could use some other material...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, we can find all sorts of bright, white things around, can't we?

choices.text: Perhaps we could go with Paimon's hair...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can't make paints outta hair!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And even if you could, you can't just pluck Paimon's!

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: "Something <color=#00E1FFFF>white</color>"... What is that?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sluasi carefully checks the material before handing them back to you...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, I see, so this is the color that you call "white," yes?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: I cannot help but feel that this is the exact opposite of what the "sun's color" is. Would its opposite, then, not be more suitable?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Its "opposite"... You mean black?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: "Black"... Yes, that must be it. "Black." A brilliant solution, esteemed Paimon. That must be the sun's color indeed!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why black, though?

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: In that case, could I ask one more thing of you two?

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Please, bring me something that is "black." That way, I shall know what material I must use to create "a color as radiant as the sun."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do we really have to look for that? Paimon thinks we're starting to veer further and further away from anything associated with the sun...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since she's asked us to... Let's go find her something that's "black," shall we?

choices.text: So if it was the sun at night...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The sun doesn't become black at night! Never mind that, there isn't even a sun at night!

choices.text: Wonderful and befitting of you, esteemed Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you cut that out!

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: If I see something <color=#00E1FFFF>black</color>, I will be able to mix a color as radiant as the sun...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sluasi carefully checks the material before handing them back to you...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Thank you very much. With this, I'm sure I shall be able to make pigments "as bright as the sun," which I may then give her as a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will this really work...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or rather, can you really make "bright colors" using such base materials?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Sluasi sure does look happy, though...

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Whatever the case, I thank you two for your help.

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Please, take these as my thanks...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sh—Shiny gems — and components, too!

response.speaker: Sluasi
response.text: Hehe. I am glad you like them. If you desire any ornaments in the future, you know where to find me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true, the colors Mamere uses are pretty weird too...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is what they call "Cor Lapis."

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, it is so warm... it smells so good and feels so soft — it truly is as gentle as the sun itself. Surely, humans must use these to make food? Anyway, thank you so much. I will remember this item.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How... were you able to see all that?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is the thing you call a "Nilotpala Lotus."

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Hmm. How strange. Why is it named for the moon, when it should be the thing "closest in color to the sun"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, are the sun and moon really that different in color?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, I see, I see... This is the "Berry" you spoke of.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: It is cold and hard, yet supple... and it stings the eyes like the sunlight of a winter afternoon. Surely this must be a metal that humans forge to make their weapons! Thank you very much. I shall remember this item.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How... were you able to see all that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, wouldn't "a metal painted white" simply be a "White Iron Chunk"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Come to think of it, considering the price difference between stone and metal, there might actually be some unscrupulous people who might paint stone to sell it as White Iron...

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Wow! It's so beautiful! And it even has a light scent to it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gathering them could be quite tough... But would that be a problem?

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's a pearl! But it feels a little different from the ones I've seen before. I sense a... coldness from it, of a sort.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. This is no ordinary pearl. It's a Sango Pearl, which means "coral pearl"!

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Hmm. Can corals produce pearls too? The outside world is truly fascinating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err... That's not exactly true. It's called that because they grow near corals.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: This is... an ordinary Iron Chunk. I see, so this is what you would term "black"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, its shade is a little off, but Paimon reckons it'll work just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Is this a bone from some creature? I see, I see. You mean to show that the "blackness" of the sun is all that remains once something has become bereft of all life...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that kind of weird stuff! Anyway, Sand Grease Pupae aren't bones, they're just the shells left behind by Quicksand Eels!

dialogues.speaker: Sluasi
dialogues.text: Ah, like taking off old clothes? I see. They are very beautiful clothes, though. Now, if only I could sew together something similar...
